content.user_title: Build Personal Tools From Real Problems
content.value_statement: Many personal workflows waste time because existing tools do not match the job. This skill helps you design, prototype, and refine focused tools that solve your own recurring problems.
actual_capabilities: Turns repeated personal tasks into focused tool ideas and prototypes.
Provides decision checks for validating whether a tool is worth building.
Outlines Node.js and Python CLI structures with common libraries.
Explains local-first storage options using JSON files, SQLite, IndexedDB, and desktop stacks.
Shows how to evolve a private script into a maintainable product candidate.
Identifies common personal-tool mistakes, including over-engineering and weak dogfooding.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a complete production application.
It does not replace secure coding review for generated tools.
Examples are generic and need adaptation for each operating system and data model.
It focuses on individual workflows more than large team collaboration.

use_cases.title: Automate a Daily Manual Task
use_cases.description: Map a repeated workflow into a small script or CLI command that saves time each day.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Local-First App
use_cases.description: Choose storage, interface, and packaging options for a private app that works offline.

use_cases.title: Turn a Script Into a Shareable Tool
use_cases.description: Add configuration, basic documentation, and safer defaults before sharing a useful internal tool.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Tool Idea
prompt_templates.prompt: List my repeated weekly tasks and identify one personal tool idea that is small enough to build first.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CLI Prototype
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simple CLI tool for this workflow. Include commands, inputs, outputs, and the smallest useful first version.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Local Storage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare JSON files, SQLite, and browser storage for my personal tool. Recommend one choice and explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Sharing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my personal tool plan for portability, configuration, security, documentation, and support risks before I share it.

output_examples.input: I copy client notes into three files every afternoon.
output: Recommended first tool: a notes collector CLI.
Core command: collect notes from a folder and create one dated summary.
First version scope: fixed folder path, plain text output, and no account system.

output_examples.input: I want a private desktop tracker for recurring maintenance tasks.
output: Suggested stack: Tauri with SQLite for a lightweight local-first app.
Data model: tasks, schedules, completions, and optional notes.
Risk to handle early: backup and export before adding more features.

output_examples.input: My script works for me, and two colleagues want to use it.
output: Next steps: replace hardcoded paths with configuration.
Add setup instructions, sample data, and clear error messages.
Keep the first shared release small and document unsupported cases.

best_practices: Start with one real workflow and build the smallest tool that completes it.
Use the tool daily before adding features for other users.
Add configuration, backup, and error handling before sharing the tool.
anti_patterns: Building for imagined users before proving that you need the tool yourself.
Adding complex architecture before the first version saves real time.
Skipping security review because the tool started as a private script.

faq.question: What kind of tools does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps with personal scripts, CLI tools, local-first apps, and automations for repeated workflows.

faq.question: Is this skill only for experienced developers?
faq.answer: No. It supports simple first versions, but users need basic coding ability to implement most examples.

faq.question: Can it help choose a technology stack?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares common CLI, desktop, browser, and local storage options for personal tools.

faq.question: Does it generate complete applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides structure, examples, and planning guidance that users adapt into working software.

faq.question: How does it handle security?
faq.answer: It reminds users to review storage, configuration, portability, and vulnerabilities before sharing a tool.

faq.question: Can a personal tool become a product?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains how to improve a useful private script before sharing it with others.
